ZEAL population analysis: proposed scope, phenotypes, and current QTL status

Planning document for group discussion. The proposed structure follows Chen et al. 2019 (TeoNAM) as a template only.

Author

Fausto Rodríguez-Zapata

Published

August 5, 2026

Purpose

This document is to align the group on the analysis scope for the ZEAL (Zea Exotic Allele Library) population before we commit to writing. It collects three things: a proposed paper structure, the phenotype inventory with current QTL counts, and a first draft of the whole-genome QTL figure. The structure borrows the shape of Chen et al. 2019 (TeoNAM), which is the closest published analog.

The phenotype panel is fixed to the measurements we already have. This document does not propose scoring any new phenotypes.

Proposed paper structure (for discussion)

Resource-first framing, with hypothesis-driven vignettes on the traits where the teosinte contrast is sharpest. Proposed, not settled:

  1. Introduction. Teosinte as a reservoir of domestication and adaptation alleles; what an exotic-allele library in a maize background offers; how ZEAL relates to and differs from TeoNAM.
  2. Materials and methods. Population and design; SNP50K plus skim genotyping and the RTIGER ancestry mosaic (cite the nilHMM methods paper, do not re-derive it); phenotyping across CLY23, CLY25, and Guadalajara; SpATS BLUEs and empirical-logit binary traits; R/qtl joint scan and MLM SNP50K.
  3. Results.
    • The resource: population, marker density, ancestry-mosaic summary.
    • Phenotypic variation: heritabilities and trait correlations across environments.
    • Genetic architecture: the whole-genome QTL figure (below).
    • Comparison with TeoNAM: the four overlapping traits (table below).
    • Hypothesis-driven vignettes: flowering time (with the North Carolina vs Guadalajara photoperiod contrast) and the ZEAL-signature qualitative traits TeoNAM never scored (StPu, StPi, Kinki, inv4m).
  4. Discussion. Resource value; what the overlap does and does not cover; novel loci.
  5. Data and resource availability. Genotype and phenotype data, tracked reproduction scripts, and the zealbrowser fragment browser.

Phenotypes we have

Fourteen mapped traits. QTL counts are computed live from the R/qtl joint scan with a taxon covariate (taxa Zv, Zx, Zl, Zd, Zh), taking one peak per chromosome (the refine-peaks multi-peak step is skipped because it over-segments). This taxon-covariate joint scan is the authoritative model for reported QTL. Counts are provisional, not final.

Trait Description Field Type QTL (joint scan) Status
DTA days to anthesis CLY23 + CLY25 SpATS BLUE 2 TeoNAM overlap
DTS days to silk CLY23 + CLY25 SpATS BLUE 2 TeoNAM overlap
PH plant height CLY23 + CLY25 SpATS BLUE 5 TeoNAM overlap
Prolif prolificacy (ears per plant) CLY23 + CLY25 SpATS BLUE 4 TeoNAM overlap
EH ear height CLY23 + CLY25 SpATS BLUE 4 mapped; not a TeoNAM trait
EN ear number CLY23 + CLY25 SpATS BLUE 7 mapped; not a TeoNAM trait
LAE leaves above ear CLY25 SpATS BLUE 3 mapped; single environment
NBR brace root number CLY23 + CLY25 SpATS BLUE 1 mapped; not a TeoNAM trait
SPAD leaf greenness (leaf N proxy) CLY25 SpATS BLUE 3 source to standardize
SPAD20DAS SPAD 20 days after sowing introfinder as measured (per line mean) 0 secondary source (introfinder)
SPAD36DAS SPAD 36 days after sowing introfinder as measured (per line mean) 2 secondary source (introfinder)
StPi stem pigment, anthocyanin (binary) CLY23 empirical logit 4 qualitative; ZEAL signature
StPu stem pubescence, macrohairs (binary) CLY23 empirical logit 0 qualitative; 0 QTL in taxon scan
Kinki zigzag culm (binary) CLY23 empirical logit 3 qualitative; single environment

EN vs Prolif. These are distinct ear-count traits (definitions in TERMINOLOGY.md): EN (ear number) counts the number of nodes that bear ears, whereas Prolif (prolificacy) counts the total number of ears per plant, so a single node bearing more than one ear adds to Prolif but not to EN. The CLY25 protocol counts every ear where a cob can be felt.

Notes on the current numbers.

  • StPu shows 0 QTL in the taxon-covariate joint scan but has peaks in the per-taxon scans. This looks like the taxon covariate absorbing the signal, and it needs understanding before StPu is reported. SPAD20DAS shows the same pattern (0).
  • Skipping the refine step returns counts to one peak per chromosome (for example EN drops from 17 refined peaks to 7). This is the authoritative setting going forward.
  • The taxon-covariate joint scan is authoritative for the reported QTL, matching the family-nested joint scan TeoNAM used, here nested on the five teosinte taxa.

Decisions still open

These are existing data or provenance cleanups, not new phenotyping.

Item Data Decision
Nitrogen content existing (Hannah) add as its own trait to the rqtl list; needs units, tissue, and field. SPAD stays as a correlated proxy, not a substitute
Guadalajara flowering existing (Ruben) add as a second environment for DTA and DTS; needs the fieldbook and a line-name crosswalk. Enables the photoperiod contrast
SPAD sourcing two lineages exist standardize on the primary CLY25 fieldbook SpATS BLUE; demote the introfinder SPAD20DAS and SPAD36DAS to secondary

Overlap with TeoNAM (Chen et al. 2019)

TeoNAM measured 22 traits: 15 domestication traits (CULM, EB, ED, EL, GLCO, GLUM, KRN, KW, LFLN, LFWD, PROL, REPE, SHN, STAM, TILN) and 7 agronomic traits (ASI, BARE, DTA, DTS, PLHT, TBN, YEPE). Of these, four are measured in ZEAL:

ZEAL Chen 2019 Trait Chen’s bucket
DTA DTA days to anthesis agronomic
DTS DTS days to silk agronomic
PH PLHT plant height agronomic
Prolif PROL prolificacy domestication (Chen scored binary presence; ZEAL scores a count)

Read honestly: three of the four overlaps are Chen’s agronomic traits and one (prolificacy) is his domestication bucket. So the comparison reads as “ZEAL recovers TeoNAM’s agronomic architecture plus one domestication trait.” The classic domestication-syndrome traits that carry TeoNAM’s headline results (shattering, glume/cupule, kernel row number, tillering) are not in the ZEAL panel, so the ZEAL contribution on the domestication side runs through the qualitative traits TeoNAM did not score (StPu, StPi, Kinki, inv4m).

Mapping software note

QTL mapping uses R/qtl (version 1) with a BC2S3 bcsft cross. We do not use R/qtl2, whose find_peaks handles multiple peaks per chromosome natively, because R/qtl2 does not support the BCsFt (backcross then selfing) cross type. R/qtl2’s cross-type set is bc, f2, riself and risib, dh, haploid, ail, do, hs, genail and genril, and magic19, with no bcsft (confirmed from the R/qtl2 source). The only workaround, computing BC2S3 genotype probabilities in R/qtl and passing that probability array to R/qtl2, is unnecessary now that we take one peak per chromosome.

Current QTL status: draft figure

Draft, scoped to the four TeoNAM-overlap traits (the same four as the comparison table above). Taxon-covariate joint scan, one peak per chromosome (refine step skipped). Produced by scripts/zeal_qtl_effects.R (per-QTL variance and effect) and scripts/fig_zeal_qtl_summary.R (the composite), reading the R/qtl joint-scan outputs.

Full-model variance explained by the mapped QTL:

Trait QTL Variance explained (%)
dta 2 5.7
dts 2 5.9
ph 5 11.2
prolif 4 14.0

Draft refinements still needed (so the group reads the figure as provisional):

  • Several support intervals are very wide (tens of Mb). The candidate-gene labels on those peaks imply a localization the intervals do not support; wide intervals should be de-emphasized or their labels dropped.
  • Candidate-label crowding near chromosomes 9 and 10 (the flowering candidate prints twice; one peak stacks three symbols). Curate to one label per locus.
  • The Prolif headline locus in panel C is a top-LOD peak with no candidate overlap; a candidate-overlapping Prolif peak (ub3, chromosome 4) may be the more meaningful headline.
  • Panel reading order and gene-symbol styling (italic, correct casing) to fix.

Open questions for the meeting

  1. Nitrogen content: units, tissue, and field, so it can be added to the rqtl list.
  2. Guadalajara flowering: fieldbook and line-name crosswalk, to add it as a second environment for DTA and DTS.
  3. Confirm SPAD is sourced from the primary CLY25 fieldbook, with the introfinder SPAD20DAS/SPAD36DAS demoted to secondary.
  4. Which traits carry the hypothesis-driven vignettes (flowering plus the qualitative teosinte traits), and how much of the paper is resource description vs those vignettes.

QTL by taxon

The taxon-covariate joint scan pools the five teosinte taxa. A separate question is which taxon contributes each QTL. TeoNAM answered the analog with a heatmap of allele effect by donor; the ZEAL analog is effect by taxon (Zv, Zx, Zl, Zd, Zh). We also run per-taxon additive scans, which show in one multicolor panel where each taxon peaks. Proposed: a paper section on the per-taxon QTL, using the effect-by-taxon summary plus the per-taxon scans.

Pigmentation (StPi, stem anthocyanin) is a clean example. Different taxa peak at different anthocyanin-pathway loci:

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(here)
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(data.table))
RQ <- here("results/sim/zeal/rqtl")

# Live QTL count = peaks in the taxon-covariate joint scan (taxa Zv, Zx, Zl, Zd, Zh),
# one peak per chromosome. We deliberately skip the refine-peaks (multi-peak) step
# because it over-segments, so counts come from the confidence-interval peak table.
count_qtl <- function(stem, model = "taxon") {
  f <- file.path(RQ, sprintf("zeal_%s_peaks_ci_%s.csv", stem, model))
  if (!file.exists(f)) return(NA_integer_)
  d <- tryCatch(fread(f), error = function(e) data.table())
  nrow(d)
}
```

## Phenotypes we have

Fourteen mapped traits. QTL counts are computed live from the R/qtl joint scan with a
taxon covariate (taxa Zv, Zx, Zl, Zd, Zh), taking one peak per chromosome (the refine-peaks
multi-peak step is skipped because it over-segments). This taxon-covariate joint scan is
the authoritative model for reported QTL. Counts are provisional, not final.

```{r}
#| label: pheno-inventory
inv <- data.table(
  Trait = c("DTA", "DTS", "PH", "Prolif", "EH", "EN", "LAE", "NBR",
            "SPAD", "SPAD20DAS", "SPAD36DAS", "StPi", "StPu", "Kinki"),
  stem  = c("dta", "dts", "ph", "prolif", "eh", "en", "lae", "nbr",
            "spad", "spad20das", "spad36das", "stpi", "stpu", "kinki"),
  Description = c(
    "days to anthesis", "days to silk", "plant height",
    "prolificacy (ears per plant)", "ear height", "ear number",
    "leaves above ear", "brace root number", "leaf greenness (leaf N proxy)",
    "SPAD 20 days after sowing", "SPAD 36 days after sowing",
    "stem pigment, anthocyanin (binary)", "stem pubescence, macrohairs (binary)",
    "zigzag culm (binary)"),
  Field = c("CLY23 + CLY25", "CLY23 + CLY25", "CLY23 + CLY25", "CLY23 + CLY25",
            "CLY23 + CLY25", "CLY23 + CLY25", "CLY25", "CLY23 + CLY25",
            "CLY25", "introfinder", "introfinder", "CLY23", "CLY23", "CLY23"),
  Type = c("SpATS BLUE", "SpATS BLUE", "SpATS BLUE", "SpATS BLUE", "SpATS BLUE",
           "SpATS BLUE", "SpATS BLUE", "SpATS BLUE", "SpATS BLUE",
           "as measured (per line mean)", "as measured (per line mean)",
           "empirical logit", "empirical logit", "empirical logit"),
  Status = c(
    "TeoNAM overlap", "TeoNAM overlap", "TeoNAM overlap", "TeoNAM overlap",
    "mapped; not a TeoNAM trait", "mapped; not a TeoNAM trait",
    "mapped; single environment", "mapped; not a TeoNAM trait",
    "source to standardize", "secondary source (introfinder)",
    "secondary source (introfinder)", "qualitative; ZEAL signature",
    "qualitative; 0 QTL in taxon scan", "qualitative; single environment")
)
inv[, `QTL (joint scan)` := vapply(stem, count_qtl, integer(1))]
inv[, stem := NULL]
setcolorder(inv, c("Trait", "Description", "Field", "Type", "QTL (joint scan)", "Status"))
knitr::kable(inv)
```

## Overlap with TeoNAM (Chen et al. 2019)

TeoNAM measured 22 traits: 15 domestication traits (CULM, EB, ED, EL, GLCO, GLUM, KRN,
KW, LFLN, LFWD, PROL, REPE, SHN, STAM, TILN) and 7 agronomic traits (ASI, BARE, DTA, DTS,
PLHT, TBN, YEPE). Of these, four are measured in ZEAL:

```{r}
#| label: overlap
ov <- data.table(
  ZEAL = c("DTA", "DTS", "PH", "Prolif"),
  `Chen 2019` = c("DTA", "DTS", "PLHT", "PROL"),
  Trait = c("days to anthesis", "days to silk", "plant height", "prolificacy"),
  `Chen's bucket` = c(
    "agronomic", "agronomic", "agronomic",
    "domestication (Chen scored binary presence; ZEAL scores a count)")
)
knitr::kable(ov)
```

Read honestly: three of the four overlaps are Chen's agronomic traits and one (prolificacy)
is his domestication bucket. So the comparison reads as "ZEAL recovers TeoNAM's agronomic
architecture plus one domestication trait." The classic domestication-syndrome traits that
carry TeoNAM's headline results (shattering, glume/cupule, kernel row number, tillering)
are not in the ZEAL panel, so the ZEAL contribution on the domestication side runs through
the qualitative traits TeoNAM did not score (StPu, StPi, Kinki, inv4m).

## Current QTL status: draft figure

Draft, scoped to the four TeoNAM-overlap traits (the same four as the comparison table
above). Taxon-covariate joint scan, one peak per chromosome (refine step skipped). Produced
by `scripts/zeal_qtl_effects.R` (per-QTL variance and effect) and
`scripts/fig_zeal_qtl_summary.R` (the composite), reading the R/qtl joint-scan outputs.

```{r}
#| label: fig-qtl
#| fig-cap: "Draft. ZEAL R/qtl joint-scan QTL for the four TeoNAM-overlap traits (DTA, DTS, PH, Prolif). A: genome-wide QTL support intervals in Mb, bar width scaled by LOD, candidate genes labeled. B: per-QTL variance explained (fitqtl drop-one). C: raw allele effect at two headline loci, phenotype BLUE by genotype class (A = B73, H = het, B = teosinte). D: variance explained by the mapped-QTL joint model."
#| out-width: 100%
knitr::include_graphics(here("results/sim/zeal/fig_zeal_qtl_summary.png"))
```

Full-model variance explained by the mapped QTL:

setnames(vp, c("trait", "n_qtl", "pct_var_qtl_model"),

## QTL by taxon

The taxon-covariate joint scan pools the five teosinte taxa. A separate question is which
taxon contributes each QTL. TeoNAM answered the analog with a heatmap of allele effect by
donor; the ZEAL analog is effect by taxon (Zv, Zx, Zl, Zd, Zh). We also run per-taxon
additive scans, which show in one multicolor panel where each taxon peaks. Proposed: a
paper section on the per-taxon QTL, using the effect-by-taxon summary plus the per-taxon
scans.

Pigmentation (StPi, stem anthocyanin) is a clean example. Different taxa peak at different
anthocyanin-pathway loci:

```{r}
#| label: fig-stpi-taxon
#| fig-cap: "ZEAL StPi (stem anthocyanin) per-taxon additive scan on the TeoNAM JLM grid. LOD by taxon (Zd, Zh, Zl, Zv, Zx); dotted verticals mark anthocyanin-pathway candidate genes (b1, a1, c2, pr1, pl1, bz1, and others). Different taxa contribute pigmentation signal at different loci, for example Zx and Zv near b1 on chromosome 2 and Zd near chromosome 8."
#| out-width: 100%
knitr::include_graphics(here("results/sim/zeal/rqtl/zeal_stpi_lod_by_taxon.png"))
```
